title: .agents/compatibility.json
description: The machine-readable declaration of a repository's agent-context layout. Never loaded into any model's context; read only by agentkit and the hooks. This is the anti-drift anchor: every claim here is asserted against the filesystem by `agentkit verify`, because a declaration nobody checks is how drift starts.

policyDraft.description: Output of `agentkit policy scaffold`. NOTHING HERE IS ENFORCED. Entries are harvested from the repo's existing gate scripts and AGENTS.md so review is cheap; a human promotes them into `policy`. Auto-enforcing a regex scraped from a shell script is how a gate ends up blocking honest work and getting disabled on the next repo.

agentkitVersion.description: Version of the kit vendored into this repo. Drives the cross-repo drift check.

canonical.description: Every path the verifier asserts exists. Paths are repo-relative and POSIX-separated.

optionalFiles.description: Canonical files that exist in this repo but are not required of every repo. `obligations.md` is the built-in case: roughly one repo in four has an external counterparty, and the rest should not carry a ceremonial empty file.

adapters.description: Every non-native reach path. The verifier resolves each one and fails on a broken link, an absolute symlink, or a target outside the canonical skills directory.

enforcement.description: Per-harness enforcement level. `blocking` is a claim that a deny actually denies, and `agentkit verify --self-test` is what makes the claim honest: it fires a known-forbidden call and asserts refusal. Do not declare blocking without it.

autoMemory.description: Declared state of Claude Code auto memory. Asserted against settings.json `autoMemoryEnabled`; a mismatch is an error. Default is `on` — Anthropic's own split puts learnings there. Set `off` where a data boundary exists, and say why in autoMemoryReason.

autoMemoryReason.description: Required when autoMemory is `off`. An unreviewed store the agent writes to unprompted is a data-at-rest surface; if that is the reason, name the data.

budgets.description: Every constant, each with its source. These live here and nowhere else so that 41 repos do not hardcode them.

codexProjectDocMaxBytes.description: HARD FAIL threshold for the Codex-visible chain. The real shipped default, not a fraction of it: gating below what is enforced buys nothing and costs real deletions from a safety file.

codexBudgetSource.description: Where the constant was read, with a commit SHA and a date. If this is stale, re-read before trusting the number.

claudeLineTarget.description: WARN threshold on the Claude-visible repo-controlled set. Anthropic publishes no byte cap, only an adherence target, and a qualitative target earns a warning rather than a build failure.

policy.description: What the mechanical gates enforce. Read at runtime by the Edit/Write and MCP hooks, and compiled into settings.json permissions.deny by `agentkit apply`. Anthropic's steer is followed here: hard tool/path blocks go to permissions.deny, and hooks carry only what permissions cannot express.

protectedBranches.description: Push to these asks; force-push to these is denied.

denyBashPatterns.description: Repo-specific Bash denials, read at runtime by the Bash gate. Harvest these with `agentkit policy scaffold` rather than writing them from scratch — a fieldbook repo's existing gate script already encodes its real fences.

pattern.description: POSIX ERE, matched against the command with grep -E

reason.description: Shown on denial. A gate that explains itself is one people fix rather than route around.

askBashPatterns.description: Same shape as denyBashPatterns, but prompts instead of refusing. For the reversible-but-consequential class.

reason.description: Shown to the agent on denial. A gate that explains itself is one people fix rather than route around.

denyWritePaths.description: Paths no agent may Edit or Write. Compiled into permissions.deny AND checked by the hook, deliberately twice: permissions.deny is the client-enforced layer, the hook is what still fires if a settings layer is missing.

pattern.description: Python regex matched against the full tool name, e.g. ^mcp__.*__deploy_to_vercel$

whenArgMatches.description: Optional narrowing: deny only when a named argument matches a regex. Lets `deploy(target=preview)` through while denying `deploy(target=production)`.

measureOnWrite.description: The external-observation gates that refusal 6 must never delete. Each entry names a path glob and a measurement to report before and after an edit. These are gates on the world, not rituals about the agent's own reasoning; deleting one removes a check that exists because a human cannot verify the output themselves.

scripts.description: Unicode script names for `script-lengths`, e.g. ["Cyrillic"]. Counted per script so a change to non-Latin text is visible to an operator who cannot read it.

fallbacks.description: What to do when a harness lacks a feature this layout assumes. Adopted from a repository that arrived at it independently and had something the kit did not: the portability story was written as 'these three harnesses support X' with nothing said about the fourth. A named degradation path is what stops a missing feature becoming an unrecorded gap.

examples.missingPlanMode: Use the active conversation plus docs/project/PLAN.md

retiredPaths.description: Globs holding content that is retired but still checked in — a fallback mirror, a superseded nested repo, an archive kept for reference. `agentkit apply` feeds these into .agnix.toml's exclude list. Without it, a retired copy of the OLD system gets linted as if it were live: on one repo a retired nested mirror produced 84 of 91 errors, which is how a finished migration reads as a failure.

harnessWritten.description: Glob allowlist of paths the harness creates itself and the verifier must tolerate. Claude Code writes real skill directories under .claude/skills (`/verify` writes verify/, `/run-skill-generator` writes run-<name>/), so a verifier that errors on any non-symlink entry breaks the first time a shipped feature is used. That bug was live in a real repository and this field is its permanent fix.

exceptions.description: The only legal place for per-repo divergence. Local cleverness in 41 places is how a system stops being one system; an exception recorded here is visible to the verifier and to the next reader.

rule.description: Which design rule is being departed from.

enforcementLevel.description: blocking = a deny is mechanically refused and a self-test proves it. advisory = the harness reads the rules but nothing stops it. none = the harness does not participate.
